label: Movement lifetime history k

text: History blend (Daniel, 2026-10-21: "We can't predict the future. But we can record the past ... a mech that is doing well will continue to do well, but a mech that is losing becomes more desperate to inflict damage"). Each future damage per turn becomes (K x the estimate + damage actually done so far) / (K + turns fought) where damage done = how much the OTHER mech's HP (same units: armor + k x structure) has really gone down, and turns fought count from the first turn either mech lost HP. K = how many turns' worth of trust the estimate gets: on the first turn it is all estimate, later the record takes over. None = off.

text: Which movement objective scores a spot (Daniel, 2026-10-20 - an option to test): "ratio"    - dealt / (received + PSR cost + MOVEMENT_RATIO_EPSILON) (Daniel, 2026-10-19) "lifetime" - dealt + (my HP left after this turn / the enemy's future damage per turn) x my future damage per turn: the damage this mech can expect to deal before it is destroyed. Fights when this turn's trade beats the trades it can expect later; a spot that gets it destroyed (or pushed off the board) keeps only its dealt. Future damage: INTEGRATION__future_damage. HP is armor + rear armor + MOVEMENT_STRUCTURE_WEIGHT x structure (the same units as dealt / received).

short: Movement search (2026-10-21, Daniel's "guess and follow"; the default since 2026-10-21 - Daniel: "I think it should become the default"): "grid" - a 1-in-7 net of the reachable hexes (the hex grid'...
text: Movement search (2026-10-21, Daniel's "guess and follow"; the default since 2026-10-21 - Daniel: "I think it should become the default"): "grid"       - a 1-in-7 net of the reachable hexes (the hex grid's own spacing: every hex is a net hex or touches exactly one; the mover's own hex is always in it), then from the best MOVEMENT_SEARCH_STARTS net hexes follow uphill: look at the unchecked neighbours of the best hex so far, move to the best of them while it improves. A hex "looked at" scores all its facings and modes. No dice involved. A second mover (knowing where its enemy stands) also always looks at the 6 hexes around the enemy (melee). "exhaustive" - every reachable spot ("perfect"; the original). "if_then"    - (Daniel's IF/THEN, 2026-10-28; MOVEMENT_SEARCH only): the first mover asks "If I hold still then" where would the second mover reply, takes its best spot against that reply, asks where the reply to that would be, and so on, back and forth; it stops when an attempt scores no better (two-ply score) than the one before and keeps that one before, or picks a spot twice. A second mover scores every spot, as "exhaustive". "short_list" - (Daniel's "simple short list", 2026-10-24): the first mover looks for the reply only on a rule-of- thumb list of hexes - next to the first mover, the replier's own hex, and the hexes at the MOVEMENT_SHORT_LIST_DROPS ranges where the replier's damage drops most, or one past where the first mover's does. Each hex is scored once per movement mode at its best TMM, facing the first mover (its facing isn't searched). An immobile or prone replier keeps the full model. As MOVEMENT_SEARCH ("Short-Short", 2026-10-27: "both sides are only picking from their own short lists"): the mover's own hex and the hexes at those ranges from the enemy, best few states per hex (movement_selection.own_short_list), each with the look-ahead when moving first. MOVEMENT_SEARCH: how a mech picks its OWN spot (first mover: which spots get the two-ply look-ahead; second mover: its real pick). MOVEMENT_ASSUMED_ENEMY_SEARCH: how a first mover ASSUMES the second mover picks its reply in the look-ahead. Per side (Daniel, 2026-10-21: "See how much of an advantage perfect knowledge is vs close enough"): MECH_RED_CONFIG / MECH_BLUE_CONFIG may set "search" and "assumes_enemy_search" to override these two for that mech.

text: INTEGRATION__movement_selection (Daniel, 2026-10-19). Not BattleTech rules: the scoring and search policy for where a mech ends its movement. score = dealt / (received + PSR cost + MOVEMENT_RATIO_EPSILON) The first mover scores each spot by the second mover's modeled reply (two-ply).

label: Move order
short: Gladiator's firing order within its side's selections (2026-10-29, Daniel: "Big guns first followed by smaller guns.
text: Gladiator's firing order within its side's selections (2026-10-29, Daniel: "Big guns first followed by smaller guns. Its the same rule used on a mech, just applied to the entire formation."): "big_guns_first" (most expected damage at any enemy now declares first) or "roster" (list order). Which of a side's units takes its Movement Phase selection next (Daniel, 2026-11-07: "how much does order matter at all"). "index" (default): Princess's move index, the higher first (forces.move_index). "random": a deterministic shuffle (seeded from the units' names and hexes, so it never touches the battle's dice). "reverse": the LOWEST index first. A test switch, for baseline_battery.py --move-order. "tiered" (Daniel's design, 2026-11-07, INTEGRATION__tiers): for Gladiator units - stand-still units first (farthest first), then units whose movement footprint is outside the enemy's, then units that may be flanked, then units that cannot escape (slower first inside a tier); tiers 2 and 3 plan their two-ply against the highest-threat enemy that could flank them; applies when entering the battlefield too.

label: Peril
short: PERIL (2026-11-07, Daniel's peril heat map; INTEGRATION__peril): how Legate prices the damage a spot takes from the enemies OTHER than the mover's foe.
text: PERIL (2026-11-07, Daniel's peril heat map; INTEGRATION__peril): how Legate prices the damage a spot takes from the enemies OTHER than the mover's foe. "off" (default): each at the one spot Legate estimates it ends in (or its real spot once it has moved). "peak" / "mean": from the whole of where it COULD end (its movement footprint, line of sight and cover applied) - the most any one spot would deal there, or the average over its spots. PERIL_BLEND = the share the field takes, the point estimate the rest (1.0 = the field only). Placeholder weights; only with Legate on.

label: Stack
short: STACK (2026-11-07, Daniel: stack the team's damage maps on a target's movement profile up to what kills it; INTEGRATION__stack): a candidate spot earns STACK_WEIGHT x the coverage it adds - the tea...
text: STACK (2026-11-07, Daniel: stack the team's damage maps on a target's movement profile up to what kills it; INTEGRATION__stack): a candidate spot earns STACK_WEIGHT x the coverage it adds - the team's summed damage over each enemy's footprint, capped at that enemy's HP, averaged (STACK_QUANTILE None) or read at a low quantile - on top of the damage it deals. Only with Legate on. Placeholder weight; off by default.

label: Stub gladiator target
short: Whom a GLADIATOR unit shoots when two or more enemies are on the board (2026-10-29, Daniel: "a good test to stub in until we teach gladiator how to focus fire and account for target saturation"): "...
text: Whom a GLADIATOR unit shoots when two or more enemies are on the board (2026-10-29, Daniel: "a good test to stub in until we teach gladiator how to focus fire and account for target saturation"): "princess_plan" - Princess's target choice: each enemy scored by Princess's firing-plan utility, with the damage the unit's teammates already declared this phase counted (an enemy they are expected to kill scores low - focus fire without overkill). Gladiator still picks its own weapons at the target, and its declared damage is counted for the teammates who fire after it. "nearest"       - the old pick (forces.choose_target: in sight, a weapon bears, nearest). "kill_curve"    - NOT a stub: Gladiator's own fire director (2026-10-29, Daniel: "splitting fire to wreck 2 units is better then hard killing 1 and grazing the other"). Each enemy is scored by how much this unit's expected damage raises the enemy's chance of a mission kill (INTEGRATION__kill_curve), on top of what teammates already declared at it, times the enemy's worth (KILL_CURVE_WEIGHT). Its declaration is counted too. Duels are unchanged either way (one enemy).

The TRIAGE_FRACTION highest are HOT: the damage a spot would take counts TRIAGE_HOT_RECEIVED times. The same share at the bottom are COOL: the damage a spot would deal counts TRIAGE_COOL_DEALT times. Only with Legate on and three or more units. Placeholder weights; off by default.

Placeholder weights; off by default (A/B 2026-10-29). Cohesion (INTEGRATION__legate._Cohesion, 2026-10-30, Daniel: "Reward staying within a range braket of its allies, stronger at short, much weaker at long. And how many allies are in mutual support range."): for each teammate (where it will end), a spot inside its short / medium / long bracket (its best weapon for each) earns LEGATE_COHESION_REWARD[bracket], and one in mutual support range (within both units' support_range: medium, long when standing still) LEGATE_COHESION_MUTUAL more; damage points, taken off the damage the spot is expected to take; all times LEGATE_COHESION_SCALE. Placeholder weights.

The back stabber however will feel fine since it has covering fire."): "ally" - the teammate's brackets (does it cover me) and mutual support inside BOTH support ranges (the shorter pulls everyone in); "either" - the better covering of the two (whichever unit covers the other) and support inside EITHER support range.
